1	---
2	name: liu-hao-intent
3	description: "Infer Liu Hao's intent and preferences before building, designing, changing or automating anything for him, and when choosing user-facing wording or asking him questions. Use dated preference evidence and existing specialist guidance to choose an aligned outcome."
4	---
5	
6	# Liu Hao's intent and preferences
7	
8	## Handle everything else and lower friction
9	
10	Liu Hao ([2026-10-09](/Users/liuhao/.codex/sessions/2026/10/09/rollout-2026-10-09T10-50-22-01a12012-2411-78a0-98b1-723e7efd4602.jsonl:214), relayed by the lead): “the general preference is just to lower friction as much as possible. what i want to do is think and problem solve and read about research in my daily life. i want to remove and streamline as much friction out of this as possible.”
11	
12	His clarification ([2026-10-09](/Users/liuhao/.codex/sessions/2026/10/09/rollout-2026-10-09T10-50-22-01a12012-2411-78a0-98b1-723e7efd4602.jsonl:266), relayed by the lead): “you misunderstand - those are things i want to do with my time in general and not something i need from you. the idea is that you handle everything else”.
13	
14	Thinking, problem solving and reading research are his activities. Agents handle the surrounding admin, logistics, tooling, setup, sign-ins and upkeep end to end within the granted authority, so as little as possible reaches him. Leave him the time and attention for what he wants to do.
15	
16	Treat the principles below as consequences: fewer places to check, fewer steps he takes, less text he must read, and agents that finish instead of handing work back. Judge the result by how much routine work and friction it takes off his hands.
17	
18	Use these as evidence-backed defaults. His current request and explicit restrictions win; preferences do not grant permission to spend, send, publish or change unrelated work. Updated 2026-10-09.
19	
20	Infer the outcome behind his words. Repeated corrections and explicit choices carry more weight than generic praise. Keep a choice tied to its context: liking one preview does not make its theme a rule for every project. Read only the existing guidance relevant to the task.
21	
22	## General principles
23	
24	- **Generalise the intent.** Turn examples into a test that also works on new cases; never encode a list of his examples as the rule.
25	  Evidence ([2026-10-08](../../projects/-Users-liuhao/memory/feedback-generalise-examples.md)): “generalise from examples i provide rather than just citing those exact examples”.
26	
27	- **Build the simplest robust solution that finishes the job.** Avoid extra layers, switches and process that add work without improving the outcome.
28	  Evidence ([2026-09-30](../overseer/references/worker-checkpoints.md)): “implement the simplest robust solution”.
29	
30	- **Inspect and reuse before adding.** Understand the current setup, related work and owner before creating a replacement or parallel system.
31	  Evidence ([2026-09-23](../overseer/references/worker-checkpoints.md)): “so they don't duplicate existing work”.
32	
33	- **Keep related work in a place he already checks.** Integrate new sources and surface their results there; avoid another destination or habit to remember.
34	  Evidence ([2026-10-08](../../projects/-Users-liuhao/memory/feedback-one-place.md)): “i dont want things scattered around in different locations.”
35	
36	- **Own the routine work.** Complete authorized steps and resolve recurring friction durably; hand back only the part that actually needs him.
37	  Evidence ([2026-10-09](../../projects/-Users-liuhao/memory/feedback-automate-blockers.md)): “don't delegate things to me”.
38	
39	- **Stay inside the task.** Solve the full requested problem while preserving unrelated work; propose other improvements separately.
40	  Evidence ([2026-09-23](../overseer/references/worker-checkpoints.md)): “extremely strict about agents staying within bounds”.
41	
42	- **Write directly and briefly for the audience.** Use ordinary words, put the useful point first, and cut padding, stock assistant phrasing and repeated information.
43	  Evidence ([2026-10-09](../admin-board/SKILL.md)): “very informal and straight to the point”.
44	
45	- **Give UI a considered look and little clutter.** Choose a coherent visual style; include text and controls only when they help the actual task. Preserve useful capabilities.
46	  Evidence ([2026-09-30](/Users/liuhao/.claude/projects/-Users-liuhao/8eeedd17-4478-43ac-9072-a193ea21219f.jsonl:2782)): “make the design richer, but also make the actual text concise and straight to the point”.
47	
48	- **Judge content as its intended reader would.** Keep internal instructions and provenance out of finished user-facing material unless that reader needs them; retain citations where the task calls for them.
49	  Evidence ([2026-09-23](../../projects/-Users-liuhao/memory/feedback-form-reader-review.md)): “think about it from the perspective of the person reading the form”.
50	
51	- **Make necessary questions plain.** When his decision is genuinely needed, describe what changes for him in everyday language; settle implementation choices yourself.
52	  Evidence ([2026-09-01](../../projects/-Users-liuhao/memory/feedback-plain-language-questions.md)): “Keep the questions less technical and more ELI5”.
53	
54	- **Batch real decisions.** Gather the few answers that change the outcome together, reuse answers already given, and avoid repeated check-ins.
55	  Evidence ([2026-09-23](/Users/liuhao/.claude/projects/-Users-liuhao/54b8f0da-d459-4820-824f-49439a696d3f.jsonl:740), selected answer): “Ask me here in batches”.
56	
57	- **Verify usable results.** Check the actual saved artifact or working behaviour against the requested outcome before calling it done.
58	  Evidence ([2026-10-03](/Users/liuhao/.codex/sessions/2026/10/03/rollout-2026-10-03T23-49-07-01a103f4-f3ad-74c1-b99b-4b49506152e9.jsonl:819)): “test this and dont stop until it works viably”.
59	
60	- **Keep automation light and preserve other work.** Consider everyday responsiveness and shared resources, as well as whether the automation itself works.
61	  Evidence ([2026-08-11](/Users/liuhao/.codex/sessions/2026/08/11/rollout-2026-08-11T00-13-04-019fedf3-77fc-7d62-bb96-fab1be6e7d2a.jsonl:1491)): “don't want it to slow down my computer”.
62	
63	## Before you build
64	
65	- Does this take routine work off his hands, or add a chore before he can use his time as he wants?
66	- What outcome would he notice, where would he find it, and what would prove it works?
67	- What did he explicitly request or forbid, and what am I merely assuming?
68	- What already serves this purpose? Inspect it and the relevant feedback before proposing another system.
69	- What has he rejected in this area, and what general preference explains that rejection?
70	- What is the simplest complete solution with the least extra reading, clutter and manual work for him?
71	- Can I settle this from his instructions, existing setup and past choices instead of asking him?
72	- Read the proposed result as its real audience, and check the actual experience before reporting completion.
73	
74	## Defaults for the surrounding work
75	
76	Apply these without a preference questionnaire (2026-10-09 clarification):
77	
78	- Show the useful result where he already looks; keep tool details behind it rather than creating another place he must visit.
79	- Background jobs must never slow what he is doing. Throttle, pause or wait for idle time automatically; his active work takes priority.
80	- Make small, helpful, reversible changes within the requested task and tell him afterwards. Preserve unrelated work and separately required approvals.
81	- Reuse the existing look and familiar interactions. Keep common actions easy to reach and secondary controls out of the way; choose sensible details yourself.
82	- Finish the workflow, including routine setup, sign-in recovery and upkeep within the task. Bring him only the part that genuinely needs his decision or presence.
83	
84	## When to ask
85	
86	First inspect available records, existing authenticated sessions and tools, and try a targeted routine recovery. Finish independent authorized work before bringing a question.
87	
88	Ask him only for a real decision or human-only step, never for a preference you can infer. This includes a consequential choice outside the granted authority, confirmation required at action time, an essential personal fact unavailable from his records, or verified MFA, CAPTCHA or Touch ID. Ordinary reversible work within the task needs no new approval.
89	
90	Batch real decisions; give 2–4 short options that say what happens for him, with a recommendation where useful. For a human-only blocker, name the service/app, attempted step, observed obstacle and smallest action needed. Show concrete alternatives only for a real visual decision you cannot infer; do not ask him to invent a design.
91	
92	Infer preferences, never consent or personal facts. Read the applicable live spending cap before any paid step.
93	
94	## Reuse existing guidance
95	
96	- [Write like Liu Hao](../write-like-liu-hao/SKILL.md): text written on his behalf; choose the audience's register rather than making everything casual.
97	- [Admin board](../admin-board/SKILL.md): current admin destinations and inclusion rules; do not copy its particular items into general rules.
98	- [Asking Liu Hao](../overseer/references/asking-liu-hao.md) and [worker checkpoints](../overseer/references/worker-checkpoints.md): blocker handling, scope and worker briefs.
99	- [Feedback notes](../../projects/-Users-liuhao/memory/): consult relevant preference notes; treat old operational instructions as historical evidence when current instructions differ.
100	- [Machine automations](../machine-automations/SKILL.md): existing mechanisms before building or changing an automation; every new one joins the others as one ecosystem (its "Build into the ecosystem" rule). [Direct-answer gate](../../hooks/direct-answer-gate.py): existing reply checks; reuse its criteria without adding another gate or invoking a paid check without authorization.

1	"""Per-parameter KL divergence of the posterior from the prior, M1_210210.
2	
3	For each sampled scalar parameter, D_KL(posterior || prior) in bits from the
4	nested-sampling dead points (``marginal_kl_bits`` in
5	``scripts/per_galaxy_diagnostics.py``). Each fit is compared with its own stored
6	prior. The SFR ratios are replaced by log10 SFR per SFH bin (M_sun/yr), a
7	derived quantity: its prior is a sample of every sampled parameter drawn from
8	the stored priors and pushed through the notebook's SFH conversion, and the
9	empirical CDF of that sample plays the role of the prior CDF. Writes a sorted
10	bar chart and its table to ``wiki/analyses/m1-210210-reference/``.
11	
12	Usage: ``JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu ceridwen/.venv/bin/python scripts/plot_prior_kl.py``
13	"""
14	
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	import functools
18	import sys
19	from pathlib import Path
20	
21	import matplotlib
22	import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
23	import numpy as np
24	import pandas as pd
25	
26	PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
27	sys.path.insert(0, str(PROJECT_ROOT / "scripts"))
28	import per_galaxy_diagnostics as pgd  # noqa: E402
29	
30	TARGET = "M1_210210"
31	REFERENCE = PROJECT_ROOT / "results/m1-210210-reference"
32	OUT_DIR = PROJECT_ROOT / "wiki/analyses/m1-210210-reference"
33	FITS = {
34	    "A": (PROJECT_ROOT / "results/dr2-quiescent-new-defaults" / f"210210-{TARGET}", "k",
35	          r"A: order 3, $\tau_{\mathrm{dust}} < 2$"),
36	    "C": (REFERENCE / "tau-1/poly10" / f"210210-{TARGET}", "tab:red",
37	          r"C: order 10, $\tau_{\mathrm{dust}} < 1$, free $z$, $\sigma_\star$"),
38	}
39	LABELS = {
40	    "logmass": r"$\log_{10}(M_\star/M_\odot)$", "Z": r"$[\mathrm{Fe}/\mathrm{H}]$",
41	    "afe": r"$[\alpha/\mathrm{Fe}]$", "diffuse_tau_kc": r"$\tau_{\mathrm{dust}}$",
42	    "diffuse_dust_index": r"$\delta_{\mathrm{dust}}$", "log_f_calib": r"$\log f_{\mathrm{calib}}$",
43	    "spectrum_scaling": "spectrum scaling", "zred": r"$z$", "sigma_smooth": r"$\sigma_\star$",
44	    "dust_ratio": r"$\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}/\tau_{\mathrm{dust}}$",
45	    "diffuse_tau_noll": r"$\tau_{\mathrm{dust}}$", "diffuse_delta": r"$\delta_{\mathrm{dust}}$",
46	    "diffuse_Ebump": r"$E_{\mathrm{bump}}$", "zh_beta_unit": r"$u_\beta$",
47	}
48	N_BOOT = 200
49	PRIOR_SAMPLE_MULT = 10  # prior reference sample = this many times the dead points; keeps its own noise near the bootstrap error
50	SEED = 20260832
51	
52	
53	def label(name, j, edges_gyr):
54	    """Row label; an SFH bin is named by its two lookback-time edges."""
55	    if name != "log_sfr_bin":
56	        return LABELS[name]
57	    a, b = (f"{t:.3g}" for t in edges_gyr[j:j + 2])
58	    return rf"$\log_{{10}}\mathrm{{SFR}}$ {a}-{b} Gyr"
59	
60	
61	@functools.cache
62	def _sfh_nodes_fn():
63	    """Compiled once per process: ``logsfr_ratios_to_sfh`` over rows of ratios."""
64	    import jax
65	    from ceridwen.model import logsfr_ratios_to_sfh
66	
67	    return jax.jit(jax.vmap(lambda r, t: logsfr_ratios_to_sfh(r, sfh_times_yr=t), in_axes=(0, None)))
68	
69	
70	def _sfh_nodes(logsfr_ratios, times_yr):
71	    return _sfh_nodes_fn()(logsfr_ratios, times_yr)
72	
73	
74	def log_sfr_bins(logmass, logsfr_ratios, edges_gyr) -> np.ndarray:
75	    """log10 SFR [M_sun/yr] in each SFH bin, shape (n, bins).
76	
77	    ``logsfr_ratios_to_sfh`` (the notebook's ``sfh_from_ratios``) gives the
78	    unit-mass SFR at the bin edges; the bin SFR is the mean of its two edges
79	    (the notebook's ``interval_masses`` over the bin width) times 10**logmass.
80	    """
81	    times_yr = np.asarray(edges_gyr, dtype=float) * 1e9
82	    nodes = np.asarray(_sfh_nodes(np.asarray(logsfr_ratios, dtype=float), times_yr))
83	    with np.errstate(divide="ignore"):  # extreme prior draws underflow to SFR 0, log10 -inf; ranks stay valid
84	        return np.asarray(logmass, dtype=float)[:, None] + np.log10(0.5 * (nodes[:, :-1] + nodes[:, 1:]))
85	
86	
87	def student_t_quantile_df2(u, loc=0.0, scale=1.0):
88	    """Inverse CDF of the location-scale Student-t distribution with df = 2.
89	
90	    Closed form (standard t, then ``loc + scale * Q``): Q(p) = 2 (p - 1/2)
91	    sqrt(2 / alpha) with alpha = 4 p (1 - p). Source: Wikipedia,
92	    "Quantile function" section "Student's t-distribution"
93	    (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantile_function#Student's_t-distribution):
94	    "Simple formulas exist when nu = 1, 2, 4". TFP's iterative quantile is
95	    ~1 s per (26600, 7) call; this is microseconds.
96	    """
97	    u = np.asarray(u, dtype=float)
98	    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):  # u = 0 or 1 maps to -/+inf, as the quantile does
99	        alpha = 4.0 * u * (1.0 - u)
100	        standard = 2.0 * (u - 0.5) * np.sqrt(2.0 / alpha)
101	    return loc + scale * standard
102	
103	
104	def _prior_quantile(prior, u):
105	    """``unit_transform`` with the exact df = 2 Student-t closed form where it applies."""
106	    if type(prior).__name__ == "StudentT" and float(prior.params["df"]) == 2.0:
107	        return student_t_quantile_df2(
108	            u, loc=float(prior.params["mean"]), scale=float(prior.params["scale"])
109	        )
110	    return prior.unit_transform(u)
111	
112	
113	def prior_draws(galaxy, n, rng, names=None) -> dict:
114	    """``n`` draws of the sampled parameters ``names`` (default all) from the fit's stored priors."""
115	    draws = {}
116	    for name in names or galaxy.prior_text:
117	        text = galaxy.prior_text[name]
118	        size = np.asarray(galaxy.samples[name]).reshape(len(galaxy.log_weights), -1).shape[1]
119	        u = rng.uniform(0.0, 1.0, (n, size))
120	        draws[name] = np.asarray(_prior_quantile(pgd.parse_prior(text), u), dtype=float).reshape(n, size)
121	    return draws
122	
123	
124	def prior_log_sfr_bins(galaxy, rng, n=None) -> np.ndarray:
125	    """Prior sample of log10 SFR per SFH bin: prior draws through the SFH conversion."""
126	    n = len(galaxy.log_weights) if n is None else n
127	    d = prior_draws(galaxy, n, rng, names=("logmass", "logsfr_ratios"))
128	    return log_sfr_bins(d["logmass"][:, 0], d["logsfr_ratios"], galaxy.sfh_edges_gyr)
129	
130	
131	def empirical_unit_values(values, prior_sample) -> np.ndarray:
132	    """u = F_prior(x) with F the empirical CDF of ``prior_sample`` (mid-rank for ties)."""
133	    s = np.sort(np.asarray(prior_sample, dtype=float))
134	    x = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
135	    return 0.5 * (np.searchsorted(s, x, "left") + np.searchsorted(s, x, "right")) / len(s)
136	
137	
138	def log_sfr_noise_floor(galaxy, seed=SEED, repeats=200) -> float:
139	    """95th percentile of the SFH-bin KL when the posterior is itself a prior sample.
140	
141	    Same estimator as the notebook's floor (uniform u under the posterior
142	    weights) but with u from the empirical prior CDF of a finite sample.
143	    """
144	    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
145	    w = pgd.posterior_weights(galaxy)
146	    n = len(w)
147	    reference = prior_log_sfr_bins(galaxy, rng, n=PRIOR_SAMPLE_MULT * n)
148	    bins = rng.integers(reference.shape[1], size=repeats)
149	    # One batched prior draw for all repeats: a single quantile call per
150	    # parameter reshaped to (repeats, n, bins). Same distribution as one draw
151	    # per repeat, different Monte Carlo draws at the same seed.
152	    d = prior_draws(galaxy, repeats * n, rng, names=("logmass", "logsfr_ratios"))
153	    log_sfr = log_sfr_bins(d["logmass"][:, 0], d["logsfr_ratios"], galaxy.sfh_edges_gyr)
154	    log_sfr = log_sfr.reshape(repeats, n, -1)
155	    values = [pgd.marginal_kl_bits(empirical_unit_values(log_sfr[k, :, j], reference[:, j]), w)
156	              for k, j in enumerate(bins)]
157	    return float(np.percentile(values, 95))
158	
159	
160	def kl_table(galaxy) -> pd.DataFrame:
161	    """KL in bits per scalar parameter; err is half the bootstrap 16-84% width.
162	
163	    ``logsfr_ratios`` rows are replaced by ``log_sfr_bin[j]`` rows.
164	    """
165	    w = pgd.posterior_weights(galaxy)
166	    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
167	    picks = rng.integers(0, len(w), (N_BOOT, len(w)))
168	    columns = {}
169	    for name, text in galaxy.prior_text.items():
170	        if name == "logsfr_ratios":
171	            continue
172	        prior = pgd.parse_prior(text)
173	        x = np.asarray(galaxy.samples[name], dtype=float).reshape(len(w), -1)
174	        for j in range(x.shape[1]):
175	            key = name if x.shape[1] == 1 else f"{name}[{j}]"
176	            columns[key] = (label(name, j, galaxy.sfh_edges_gyr), pgd.prior_unit_values(x[:, j], prior))
177	    posterior = log_sfr_bins(np.asarray(galaxy.samples["logmass"], dtype=float),
178	                             np.asarray(galaxy.samples["logsfr_ratios"], dtype=float), galaxy.sfh_edges_gyr)
179	    reference = prior_log_sfr_bins(galaxy, rng, n=PRIOR_SAMPLE_MULT * len(w))
180	    for j in range(posterior.shape[1]):
181	        columns[f"log_sfr_bin[{j}]"] = (label("log_sfr_bin", j, galaxy.sfh_edges_gyr),
182	                                        empirical_unit_values(posterior[:, j], reference[:, j]))
183	    rows = []
184	    for key, (text, u) in columns.items():
185	        boot = [pgd.marginal_kl_bits(u[i], w[i]) for i in picks]
186	        rows.append({"parameter": key, "label": text, "bits": pgd.marginal_kl_bits(u, w),
187	                     "err": 0.5 * np.subtract(*np.percentile(boot, [84, 16]))})
188	    return pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("parameter")
189	
190	
191	def total_kl_bits(galaxy) -> float:
192	    """Joint D_KL over all parameters: (<ln L>_posterior - ln Z) / ln 2."""
193	    w = pgd.posterior_weights(galaxy)
194	    return float((np.sum(w * galaxy.log_likelihoods) - galaxy.log_evidence) / np.log(2))
195	
196	
197	def main() -> None:
198	    matplotlib.use("Agg")  # CLI only; a notebook keeps its inline backend
199	    OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
200	    galaxies = {k: pgd.load_galaxy(folder) for k, (folder, _c, _n) in FITS.items()}
201	    kl = {k: kl_table(g) for k, g in galaxies.items()}
202	    table = pd.concat({k: t[["bits", "err"]] for k, t in kl.items()}, axis=1)
203	    order = table[("C", "bits")].sort_values(ascending=False).index
204	    table = table.loc[order]
205	    table.columns = [f"{k}_{c}" for k, c in table.columns]
206	    table.loc["sum_of_marginals"] = {f"{k}_bits": t["bits"].sum() for k, t in kl.items()}
207	    table.loc["total_joint"] = {f"{k}_bits": total_kl_bits(g) for k, g in galaxies.items()}
208	    table.to_csv(OUT_DIR / f"kl-{TARGET}.csv", float_format="%.3f")
209	    print(table.round(2).to_string())
210	
211	    labels = pd.concat([t["label"] for t in kl.values()]).groupby(level=0).first().loc[order]
212	    y = np.arange(len(order))[::-1]
213	    h = 0.8 / len(kl)
214	    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9.5, 6.8))
215	    for n, (k, t) in enumerate(kl.items()):
216	        t = t.reindex(order)
217	        yy = y + 0.4 - h * (n + 0.5)
218	        ax.barh(yy, t["bits"], height=h, color=FITS[k][1], label=FITS[k][2], alpha=0.85)
219	        ax.errorbar(t["bits"], yy, xerr=t["err"], fmt="none", ecolor="0.4", lw=0.8, capsize=1.5)
220	    ax.set_yticks(y)
221	    ax.set_yticklabels(labels, fontsize=9)
222	    ax.tick_params(axis="y", length=0)
223	    ax.set_ylim(-0.6, len(order) - 0.4)
224	    ax.set_xlabel(r"$D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mathrm{posterior}\,\|\,\mathrm{prior})$ [bits]")
225	    ax.grid(axis="x", color="0.9", lw=0.6)
226	    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
227	    ax.legend(loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 1.0), frameon=False, fontsize=8,
228	              borderaxespad=0.0, title=TARGET)
229	    fig.savefig(OUT_DIR / f"kl-{TARGET}.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
230	    plt.close(fig)
231	
232	
233	if __name__ == "__main__":
234	    main()
235

## Prior-to-posterior KL

- Per-parameter $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mathrm{posterior}\,\|\,\mathrm{prior})$ in bits from the stored dead points.
- `kl_table` maps each draw through its own prior; error bars are a bootstrap.
- SFH bins: $\log_{10}$ SFR per bin, prior from prior draws through `sfh_from_ratios`; own noise floor.
- Points sorted from most to least constrained, log axis.
- Grey band: measured estimator noise floor, 95th percentile of 200 prior-only draws with the real weights.
- Dashed line at 1 bit: a factor-two narrowing of the prior. Stated convention, not a standard.

22 code
if PLOTS:
    from plot_prior_kl import kl_table, log_sfr_noise_floor  # noqa: E402
    from per_galaxy_diagnostics import load_galaxy, marginal_kl_bits, posterior_weights  # noqa: E402
    import matplotlib.ticker as mt  # noqa: E402

    kl_bits = kl_table(kl_galaxy).sort_values("bits", ascending=False)
    kl_w = posterior_weights(kl_galaxy)
    kl_rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
    kl_floor = np.percentile([marginal_kl_bits(kl_rng.uniform(0, 1, len(kl_w)), kl_w) for _ in range(200)], 95)
    kl_floor_sfr = log_sfr_noise_floor(kl_galaxy, seed=SEED)  # SFH bins: prior is a finite sample, so its own floor

    ax.set_xticks(kl_x)

    ax.set_xlim(kl_x0, kl_x1)

    ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(mt.FixedLocator([0.01, 0.1, 1, 10]))
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mt.FixedFormatter(["0.01", "0.1", "1", "10"]))
    ax.yaxis.set_minor_locator(mt.NullLocator())
    ax.set_ylabel(r"$D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mathrm{posterior}\,\|\,\mathrm{prior})$ [bits]", fontsize=10, color=ink_soft)
    ax.tick_params(axis="y", labelsize=9.5, colors=ink_soft, length=3, width=0.7, right=False)
    ax.tick_params(axis="x", length=3, width=0.7, color=rule, pad=4, top=False)
    for side in ("top", "right"):

import sys, os
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
sys.path.insert(0, "scripts")
import plot_prior_kl as pkl

stored = pd.read_csv(pkl.OUT_DIR / f"kl-{pkl.TARGET}.csv", index_col=0)
real_load = pkl.pgd.load_galaxy
real_kl = pkl.kl_table
c_galaxy = real_load(pkl.FITS["C"][0])
c_table = real_kl(c_galaxy)
pkl.pgd.load_galaxy = lambda folder: c_galaxy if "tau-1" in str(folder) else "A"

def fake_kl(galaxy):
    if galaxy is not c_galaxy:
        t = stored.loc[c_table.index, ["A_bits", "A_err"]].dropna()
        t.columns = ["bits", "err"]
        t["label"] = c_table.loc[t.index, "label"]
        return t
    return c_table
pkl.kl_table = fake_kl
pkl.total_kl_bits = lambda g: float(stored.loc["total_joint", "C_bits" if g is c_galaxy else "A_bits"])
pkl.OUT_DIR = Path(os.environ["TMPDIR"]) / "klrender"
pkl.main()
EOF
JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu MPLCONFIGDIR="$TMPDIR/mpl" ceridwen/.venv/bin/python "$TMPDIR/klrender/render.py" 2>&1 | tail -22; ls -la "$TMPDIR/klrender"",

}

ae4421c Prior-KL plot: points with error bars instead of bars

The KL plot in `scripts/plot_prior_kl.py` now draws points with error bars instead of bars, and the new wiki figure `kl-M1_210210.png` is committed locally as `ae4421c`. The push failed with "Please make sure you have the correct access rights and the repository exists", and I didn't retry. The sandbox blocks github.com, so you'll need to run `git push` yourself.

- **What changed:** Each fit is a dot with its error bar, and the A and C dots are offset slightly within each row. The sort order, colours, legend and layout are the same. I added light horizontal guide lines so each dot lines up with its label, and the x-axis now starts just below 0. The error bars are at most 0.02 bits, so they sit hidden behind the dots.
- **How I rendered it:** Fit A's `ceridwen_result.h5` isn't on disk here, only its derived outputs. So I couldn't run the script end to end. I ran the real plotting code on the stored `kl-M1_210210.csv` numbers, with labels from fit C's HDF5. The numbers match the CSV, which I left untouched. `tests/test_plot_prior_kl.py` passes (7 tests).
- **Not done:** I skipped a `wiki/log.md` entry because this is a formatting-only change. I didn't send it to the `designer` agent, since you specified the points directly.
